app_desc.message: Let an MCP client (Claude Code, Codex, …) operate your real Chrome — your tabs and logins. You approve new sites and risky actions.

opt_subtitle.message: All changes are saved instantly. Adjust security-related switches with care.

opt_cdp_title.message: Route all page operations through CDP (chrome.debugger)

opt_cdp_desc.message: When enabled, all page operations use CDP (chrome.debugger) instead of injecting content scripts; this allows page_eval to run on strict-CSP sites (such as Bing). Disabled by default (ADR-0017).

opt_cdp_warn.message: ⚠ When enabled, Chrome persistently displays a "Debugging this browser" banner at the top (the debugger stays attached the whole time), and the access surface is larger. Only enable this when you need to bypass CSP or want unified deep control.

opt_tools_sub.message: For any unchecked tool, an AI call receives a "tool disabled in settings" error. Note: the AI can still see that the tool exists, but cannot execute it.

opt_allowall_desc.message: When enabled, the AI can operate on any http(s) site directly, without a per-site authorization prompt for each new site. Enabling it requests the "<all_urls>" host permission. Suitable when you trust the AI to browse fully automatically; otherwise it's recommended to keep this off and use the per-site allowlist below.

opt_allowall_warn.message: ⚠ When enabled, any site (including banking, email, and intranet sites) can be operated on without authorization. Use with care.

opt_add_format.message: Format: https://domain/*. After adding manually, Chrome's host-permission prompt still needs to be approved on first visit to that site.

status_disconnected.message: Not connected (is your MCP client running?)

toast_precise_body.message: About to run a precise page scan — Chrome will show a 'Debugging' banner at the top that disappears automatically after the scan (about 1 second).
